key_insight: TRACER predicted future diagnoses across external health systems; at 95% specificity, flagged patients were up to eight times more likely than unselected patients to receive a diagnosis within one year.
clinical_relevance: EHR-based risk prediction could help target disease screening, but detection and false-alert burden vary by disease and health system.
method: Decoder-based foundation model trained on longitudinal electronic health records.
Pretrained on over 4.5 million patients from four health systems.
Evaluated 16 incident diseases at 1-, 2-, and 5-year horizons, emphasizing low false-positive rates.
evidence_signal: External evaluation included more than 2 million patients from two health systems excluded from development, with discrimination retained across systems.
watch_item: Stable overall discrimination did not ensure consistent detection or false-alert burden, underscoring the need for local evaluation before clinical use.
paper_title: TRACER, a time-to-event EHR foundation model for disease detection across health systems
